nodes.content: Develop domain-generalization methods that distinguish transferable predictive features from spurious features without source-domain annotations or target-domain data.
requirements: Achieve ≥5 percentage points higher worst-domain accuracy than ERM under unseen combinations of spurious correlations.
Keep average source-domain accuracy within one percentage point of ERM while preserving genuinely predictive features.

nodes.content: CIFS adversarially partitions examples using cross-fitted ERM residuals into label-balanced pseudo-environments, penalizes feature drift, and distills ERM logits.
Can CIFS’s residual-based pseudo-environments expose coupled color–texture shortcuts without penalizing predictive shape features?
On ShapeColorTexture-8 unseen color–texture combinations, CIFS beats ERM by ≥5 worst-domain points, losing ≤1 point in source and shape-probe accuracy.
Generate ShapeColorTexture-8 splits; train CIFS and ERM without domain labels; compare unseen-combination worst-domain, source, and shape-probe accuracy.
Run five-seed ShapeColorTexture-8 CIFS–ERM trials without domain labels or target access; measure held-out worst-domain, source, and shape-probe accuracies.
Across five ShapeColorTexture-8 seeds, CIFS worst-domain accuracy averaged 55.3% versus ERM’s 53.1%, missing the hypothesized five-point gain.
Crossed color–texture swaps added to CIFS pseudo-environments should raise worst-domain gain from 2.2 to ≥5 points with ≤1-point source/shape-probe loss.
Run five-seed ShapeColorTexture-8 CIFS with source-derived crossed color–texture swaps; compare held-out worst-domain, source, and shape-probe accuracy against ERM.
Across five ShapeColorTexture-8 seeds, swapped CIFS versus ERM: worst-domain 59.0%/53.1%, source 88.6%/89.2%, shape-probe 85.1%/85.4%.
Adopt swapped CIFS over residual-only CIFS: worst-domain gains rise from 2.2 to 5.9 points, preserving source and shape accuracy.
CIFS-Swap v1 release contains the adopted swap configuration and five-seed ShapeColorTexture-8 accuracy tables against ERM.
Run five-seed ShapeColorTexture-8 shape-only and color–texture-only probes on original CIFS versus ERM; measure source accuracy without domain labels.
Original CIFS versus ERM: shape-probe 82.8%/85.4%, color–texture-probe 75.0%/80.2%, source 88.7%/89.2%; shape loss exceeds one point.
Does CIFS-Swap preserve predictive texture when class identity depends on texture, rather than shape, without domain labels?
Train CIFS-Swap and ERM on five-seed TextureLabel-8, where texture defines class; compare source, texture-probe, and unseen-combination worst-domain accuracy.
On TextureLabel-8, CIFS-Swap/ERM achieved worst-domain 82.3%/76.6%, source 88.4%/89.0%, and texture-probe 86.2%/86.5% across five seeds.
FACTOR-Guard uses cross-fitted cue-ablation tests to protect label-essential shape or texture, swapping only unprotected factors during source-only training.
Can FACTOR-Guard protect label-essential texture without mistakenly protecting correlated color when both predict source labels?
On TextureLabel-8, FACTOR-Guard protects texture but not color, gaining ≥5 worst-domain points over ERM with ≤1-point source/texture-probe loss.
Extend CIFS-Swap v1 with FACTOR-Guard; audit texture/color protection and compare five-seed TextureLabel-8 worst-domain, source, texture-probe accuracy against ERM.
Across five TextureLabel-8 seeds, FACTOR-Guard/ERM achieved worst-domain 83.1%/76.6%, source 88.6%/89.0%, and texture-probe 86.3%/86.5%; texture/color protection rates were 94%/9%.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, stress-test FACTOR-Guard at 95% source color–texture agreement; audit cue protection and worst-domain, source, texture-probe accuracy.
At 95% source color–texture agreement on TextureLabel-8, FACTOR-Guard protected color 62% and improved worst-domain accuracy only 3.1 points over ERM.
Texture-fixed recoloring should cut 95%-agreement color protection from 62% to <15%, yielding ≥5-point worst-domain gain with ≤1-point source/texture-probe losses.
Modify CIFS-Swap v1 with texture-fixed recoloring; rerun five-seed 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8, auditing cue protection and ERM-relative worst-domain, source, texture-probe accuracy.
At 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8, recoloring cut color protection to 11%, but gained only 4.2 worst-domain points versus ERM.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, sweep texture-fixed recoloring probabilities (25%, 50%, 100%) at 95% agreement; measure worst-domain gain and source/texture-probe retention.
On five-seed 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8, 50% recoloring yielded 12% color protection, +5.4-point worst-domain accuracy, −0.6-point source, −0.3-point texture-probe versus ERM.
At 95% agreement, 50% texture-fixed recoloring should sustain ≥5-point worst-domain gains, <15% color protection, and ≤1-point source/texture-probe losses.
Validate 50% recoloring across five new 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8 splits; audit color protection and ERM-relative worst-domain, source, texture-probe accuracy.
Test CIFS-Swap v1 with 50% recoloring on five fresh 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8 splits; measure color protection and ERM-relative worst-domain/source/texture-probe accuracies.
Across five fresh 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8 splits, 50% recoloring yielded 13% color protection, +5.2-point worst-domain, −0.7-point source, −0.4-point texture-probe versus ERM.
Audit CIFS-Swap v1 per-seed color protection and ERM accuracy gaps across five new 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8 splits with 50% recoloring.
On one fresh 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8 split, 50% recoloring protected color 21% and gained only 3.6 worst-domain points versus ERM.
Escalating recoloring to 75% when 50% protects color ≥15% should achieve <15% protection, ≥5-point worst-domain gains, ≤1-point source/texture-probe losses.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, trigger 75% recoloring at ≥15% source-audited color protection; compare five-split 95%-agreement TextureLabel-8 accuracies against ERM.
Across five 95%-agreement splits, adaptive 50%/75% recoloring achieved ≤14% color protection, ≥5.1-point worst-domain gains, and ≤0.9-point source/texture-probe losses.
Adopt adaptive 50%/75% recoloring: fixed 50% averaged +5.2 points but failed one split; adaptation met thresholds across all five.
FACTOR-Guard v2 packages adopted 15%-triggered adaptive recoloring, source-only cue audits, and five-split TextureLabel-8 evaluation tables.
COMBI-Guard detects spurious feature conjunctions through source-only conditional permutation tests, penalizing interactions rather than individual cues under ERM-fidelity constraints.
On XOR-ShapeTexture-8, can COMBI-Guard remove spurious color×background conjunctions while retaining label-essential shape×texture interactions?
On XOR-ShapeTexture-8, suppressing color×background interactions should yield ≥5-point worst-domain gains with ≤1-point source and shape×texture-probe losses versus ERM.
Add COMBI-Guard conditional pair permutations to FACTOR-Guard v2 audits; evaluate five-seed XOR-ShapeTexture-8 worst-domain, source, shape×texture-probe accuracies against ERM.
Five-seed XOR-ShapeTexture-8: COMBI-Guard/ERM worst-domain 67.2%/61.4%, source 89.1%/89.7%, shape×texture-probe 84.3%/84.8%; color×background/shape×texture suppression rates 82%/6%.
Adopt COMBI-Guard for XOR-ShapeTexture-8: +5.8-point worst-domain gain with 0.6-point source and 0.5-point interaction-probe losses.
COMBI-Guard v1 adds conditional interaction-permutation audits and suppression masks to FACTOR-Guard v2, with five-seed XOR-ShapeTexture-8 results.
RISK-Envelope adversarially reweights source examples by feature conjunction, optimizing worst-case accuracy within an ERM source-accuracy trust region.
On NoisyTriple-8, can RISK-Envelope upweight rare color×background conjunctions without amplifying mislabeled examples or degrading predictive shape×texture interactions?
At 10% noise, RISK-Envelope gains ≥5 worst-domain points versus ERM, loses ≤1 source/shape×texture-probe point, and limits mislabeled/clean weights to 1.2×.
Implement RISK-Envelope atop CIFS-Swap v1; test five-seed NoisyTriple-8 at 10% noise for worst-domain/source/interaction-probe accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
Five-seed NoisyTriple-8: RISK-Envelope/ERM worst-domain 66.8%/61.2%, source 85.1%/85.7%, shape×texture-probe 82.4%/82.8%; mislabeled/clean weight ratio 1.13×.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, test RISK-Envelope on five fresh 10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits with 2% rare conjunctions; audit accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
At 2% rare conjunctions, RISK-Envelope gained only 3.4 worst-domain points and assigned mislabeled examples 1.47× clean weights.
Cross-fitted loss trimming and count smoothing should yield ≥5-point worst-domain gains at 2% rarity, noisy/clean weights ≤1.2×, ≤1-point source/probe losses.
With CIFS-Swap v1, test cross-fitted trimming and count smoothing on five 2%-rarity, 10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits; audit worst-domain/source/probe accuracy, noisy/clean weights.
Five-seed NoisyTriple-8 at 2%-rarity/10%-noise: trimmed-smoothed RISK-Envelope gained 5.3 worst-domain points; noisy/clean weights 1.14×, source/probe losses 0.6/0.4 points.
Re-run CIFS-Swap v1 trimmed-smoothed RISK-Envelope on five independent 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits; audit per-split gains, source/probe losses, noisy/clean weights.
On one independent 2%-rarity NoisyTriple-8 split, trimmed-smoothed RISK-Envelope gained only 4.1 worst-domain points; noisy/clean weight ratio stayed 1.16×.
Shrink conjunction weights toward cross-fitted cue marginals to attain ≥5-point worst-domain gains at 2%-rarity, ≤1-point source/probe losses, ≤1.2× noisy/clean weights.
Tune marginal-shrinkage strength on source-only folds, then test independent 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits against ERM and trimmed-smoothed RISK-Envelope.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, tune marginal-shrinkage strength on source folds; test five independent 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits against ERM.
Across five independent 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits, shrinkage yielded ≥5.1-point worst-domain gains, ≤0.8-point source/probe losses, ≤1.17× noisy/clean weights.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, ablate marginal shrinkage on five 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits; compare worst-domain/source/probe accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
On one ablation-cohort 2%-rarity NoisyTriple-8 split, shrinkage gained only 4.4 worst-domain points versus ERM; unshrunk weighting gained 5.0.
Gate shrinkage by source-fold conjunction reliability; predict ≥5-point worst-domain gains, ≤1-point source/probe losses, and ≤1.2× noisy/clean weights.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, test reliability-gated shrinkage on five 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits; measure worst-domain/source/probe accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
Five 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits: gated shrinkage delivered ≥5.0-point worst-domain gains, ≤0.9-point source/probe losses, ≤1.18× noisy/clean weights.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, blind-test reliability-gated shrinkage across five fresh 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits; audit per-split accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
On one blind NoisyTriple-8 split, gated shrinkage gained only 4.6 worst-domain points versus ERM, despite 1.15× noisy/clean weights.
Add source-only color/background swaps to gated shrinkage for rare conjunctions; predict ≥5-point worst-domain gains, ≤1-point source/probe losses, ≤1.2× noisy/clean weights.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, augment gated shrinkage with source-only color/background swaps; test five blind 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits against ERM.
Five blind 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits: swaps plus gated shrinkage gained ≥5.1 worst-domain points; source/probe losses ≤0.8 points, noisy/clean weights ≤1.17×.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, replicate swaps plus gated shrinkage on five fresh 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits; audit worst-domain/source/probe accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
On one fresh NoisyTriple-8 split, swaps plus gated shrinkage gained 5.2 worst-domain points but lost 1.4 shape×texture-probe points.
Anchoring shape×texture logits across swaps should yield ≥5-point worst-domain gains, ≤1-point source/probe losses, and ≤1.2× noisy/clean weights.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, stratify swapped gated-shrinkage NoisyTriple-8 runs by shape×texture class; audit probe losses and ERM-relative worst-domain gains.
Four fresh NoisyTriple-8 splits showed ≥5-point worst-domain gains and ≤0.9-point shape×texture-probe losses across classes.
Using CIFS-Swap v1, add cross-swap shape×texture-logit anchoring; test five fresh 2%-rarity/10%-noise NoisyTriple-8 splits against ERM.
Fresh NoisyTriple-8 split: anchoring lost 0.5 probe points but gained only 4.7 worst-domain points versus ERM.
Using CIFS-Swap v1 and prior audits, rerun swapped/anchored gated shrinkage on matched NoisyTriple-8 splits; measure worst-domain/source/probe accuracy and noisy/clean weights.
Across matched NoisyTriple-8 splits, swaps/anchoring gained 5.2/4.8 worst-domain points but lost 1.3/0.6 shape×texture-probe points versus ERM.
Defer RISK-Envelope despite earlier successes: matched swaps lose 1.3 probe points; anchoring gains only 4.8 worst-domain points.
RISK-Envelope audit v1 records matched NoisyTriple-8 swap/anchoring comparisons and deferral: no variant meets both worst-domain and probe thresholds.
